plain_english_policy: This bill creates a new Community Development Fund for Lauderdale County using existing TVA tax payments. It establishes a Commission to manage funds for economic development, education, recreation, conservation, and fire protection. The fund's money will be split: two-thirds goes to the Commission and one-third goes to an Agriculture Authority once that authority is created.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would create a new local funding mechanism in Lauderdale County by amending Section 45-39-90 of the Code of Alabama. It establishes a Community Development Fund financed by TVA tax payments and creates a Commission to distribute funds for specific community purposes (economic development, education, recreation, conservation, fire protection). Crucially, it mandates that once an agriculture authority is established in the county, two-thirds of fund proceeds go to the existing commission while one-third goes to this new agriculture authority.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Morrow (N & P) sponsored this bill affirmatively advancing Lauderdale County's community development funding structure and the creation of an Agriculture Authority share in existing funds.
evidence_quotes: The commission may receive and by majority vote distribute any funds in the Community Development Fund created pursuant to subsection (d) for the purposes of promoting economic development, education, recreation, conservation, and fire protection.

however, after the establishment of an agriculture authority in the county, two-thirds of the proceeds shall be distributed to the commission and one-third of the proceeds shall be distributed to the authority.
